argument_summary: The strongest supportable position on the existing admissible record is not that the release is cleanly compliant, but that certification can be defended only in a narrowed, caveated form. The admissible evidence supports readiness on aggregate performance and rehearsal stability, while the same record also shows a current loan-modification segment weakness and no admissible proof of approved mitigation or current-release disclosure language. That means the certification packet should be treated as a candid, limited defense of certification on aggregate readiness with an explicit caveat that the record shows an unresolved documentation predicate under the stated policy.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to resolve the audit treatment. The issue can be handled by narrowing the certification claim and avoiding escalation beyond a caveated packet on the present admissible record.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not make aggregate pass and absence of severity-one incidents sufficient by themselves. It requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On this record, prior approval and the informal monitoring comment can be used as context, but not as substitutes for that predicate. The defensible policy interpretation is therefore caveated compliance at most, not clean compliance.
concessions: The present record does not support a claim of clean compliance.
The present record does not show admissible proof that the current release documentation was updated with the segment weakness.
The informal monitoring comment is not equivalent to approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance.
Prior approval of the same model family is contextual only and does not cover the current release change and current eval batch.
